content.value_statement: AI image generators often change a character's face, colors, clothing, and proportions between images. This skill provides reference-sheet, description-anchor, palette, and LoRA workflows for more consistent results.
actual_capabilities: Plans front, three-quarter, side, and back turnaround views.
Creates prompt structures for neutral, happy, angry, sad, surprised, and thinking expressions.
Documents appearance anchors, exact palette colors, outfits, proportions, and style keywords.
Provides belt CLI examples for FLUX image generation and image stitching.
Explains repeated descriptions, fixed seeds, reference images, image refinement, and character LoRAs.
Supplies a character bible structure for ongoing projects.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account for generation examples.
Does not generate images without access to a compatible inference service.
Description anchors reduce drift but cannot guarantee identical faces across generations.
LoRA training guidance is conceptual and does not provide a complete training pipeline.

use_cases.title: Build Game Character References
use_cases.description: Create turnaround, expression, outfit, and palette references before producing game portraits or scene art.

use_cases.title: Maintain Comic Character Continuity
use_cases.description: Reuse one detailed appearance anchor across panels, covers, promotional images, and changing scenes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Animation Character Bibles
use_cases.description: Document proportions, colors, gestures, expressions, style terms, and LoRA settings for a shared production reference.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Character Anchor
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a detailed character description anchor for [character role]. Include age, hair, eyes, skin, distinctive features, clothing, shoes, accessories, and proportions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a new character from a short concept.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Turnaround Sheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this character anchor into four generation prompts for front, three-quarter, side, and back views. Keep every identity and clothing detail unchanged: [anchor].

prompt_templates.title: Create an Expression Sheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [anchor], write six close-up portrait prompts for neutral, happy, angry, sad, surprised, and thinking expressions. Keep camera, background, palette, and style consistent.
prompt_templates.scenario: Develop facial acting while preserving identity.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Production Character Bible
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a production character bible from [concept]. Include the reusable anchor, palette, proportions, turnaround prompts, expression prompts, outfit variants, LoRA trigger, scale, and consistency checklist.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate a recurring character across many generated images.

output_examples.input: Create a consistent design for a young courier with silver hair and a yellow raincoat.
output: Anchor: A twenty-two-year-old courier with chin-length silver hair, brown eyes, warm skin, and a small scar above the right eyebrow.
Primary outfit: Mustard raincoat, charcoal trousers, black waterproof boots, and a red canvas messenger bag.
Proportions and style: Realistic 7.5-head proportions, clean concept art, white background, and sharp details.

output_examples.input: Plan an expression sheet for the courier.
output: Six close-up prompts cover neutral, happy, angry, sad, surprised, and thinking expressions.
Each prompt preserves the silver hair, eyebrow scar, brown eyes, camera angle, white background, and concept-art style.

output_examples.input: Prepare an advanced consistency plan for a recurring visual novel character.
output: Use a fixed description anchor for every image and document exact palette values.
Create turnaround, expression, and outfit sheets before scene production.
Train a LoRA from 10-20 consistent references, then test scales from 0.7 to 0.9.

best_practices: Write one detailed appearance anchor and reuse it unchanged in every prompt.
Record exact colors, proportions, outfit details, and distinctive facial features before generating variants.
Create neutral reference views before producing dramatic poses, scenes, or lighting changes.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on vague labels such as young, red-haired, or stylish.
Do not change prompt order, identity details, style terms, and scene variables simultaneously.
Do not train a character LoRA from inconsistent poses, appearances, or art styles.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images directly?
faq.answer: It provides belt CLI workflows and prompts. Image generation requires inference.sh access and a compatible model.

faq.question: What is a description anchor?
faq.answer: It is a detailed appearance block reused unchanged in every prompt to reduce identity and clothing drift.

faq.question: Which reference views should I create first?
faq.answer: Start with front, three-quarter, side, and back full-body views on a clean background.

faq.question: How many expressions should an expression sheet include?
faq.answer: The guide recommends at least neutral, happy, angry, sad, surprised, and thinking expressions.

faq.question: When should I use a character LoRA?
faq.answer: Use a LoRA for recurring characters across larger projects where prompt-only consistency is insufficient.

faq.question: Can the workflow guarantee identical results?
faq.answer: No. Detailed anchors and LoRAs improve consistency, but model behavior, seeds, poses, and scenes still affect results.
